title: Objective
text: You wake up in the crew quarters and something is wrong with the station. Walk the corridor to the Power, Oxygen, Comms and Cooling rooms, repair all four systems before the oxygen reserve runs out, then walk back to the reboot terminal at the west end of the corridor.

title: What ORACLE Can Help With
text: Ask me about the Power breakers, the Oxygen valves, the Comms frequency, the Cooling flow, protocols A and B, scoring, retrying, or the controls. For example: How do I fix the power breakers? What are the oxygen valve settings? What frequency should I transmit?

title: How to Start
text: Read the checklist at the top left and note the protocol. Leave the crew quarters and walk east to the Power room. Read its panel, look up the rule in these manuals and repair it. The next door opens once the system before it is repaired. When all four are repaired, walk back west and press E on the reboot terminal, then enter its code.

title: Hints
text: Open ORACLE with H and press the Get a hint button. On Engineer a hint costs 20 seconds of oxygen reserve. It names the next system to repair and which protocol rules apply this shift, but it never gives the answer: you still read the room's panel. Typing the word hint to ORACLE does not use a hint. On Engineer every ORACLE question also costs 5 seconds; the manuals (M) are free.

title: Station Protocol
text: Every shift runs under PROTOCOL A or B, shown on the sign in the crew quarters and in the checklist at the top left of the screen. The protocol changes the Power breaker order, the Oxygen valve table, the Comms frequency formula and the Cooling flow formula, so always check it before you repair a system. Shift 1 always uses Protocol A.

title: Controls
text: WASD moves and the mouse looks. Press E to use the terminal you are aiming at. Press M to open these manuals and H to ask ORACLE, the help assistant. Press Esc to pause, or to close a panel. Hold R for one second to retry the shift.

title: Settings
text: Open Settings from the main menu (top right) or the pause menu. Set the music and effects volume, the mouse speed, and rebind any key: click it, then press the new key (Esc cancels, and a key already in use is refused). Colour-blind cues add a cross or tick beside each room name and the words GAS: SAFE, SOON or DANGER. Sound captions show a line of text for alarms and hazards, and always show when sound is muted. Settings are saved.

title: Oxygen Reserve
text: On the Engineer level (the standard game), shift 1 starts with 360 seconds (6 minutes) of oxygen reserve. Each later shift has 45 seconds less, down to a minimum of 180 seconds. The countdown starts when you first move, and it stops while the game is paused or the manuals or ORACLE are open. If it reaches zero the shift is lost.

title: Scoring
text: When you reboot the station with all four systems repaired, your shift score is 300 plus half of your remaining reserve seconds (rounded down), minus 50 for each retry (the retry penalty is capped at 150). The highest possible score is 480, on shift 1. Mistakes already cost reserve time, so they have no separate score penalty. Level and modifiers change it (see those entries). Your run total adds up every shift you clear.

title: Retry and Next Shift
text: Hold R for one second, or choose Retry Shift in the pause menu, to restart the same station with that shift's full reserve (360 seconds on shift 1). Each retry costs 50 points. The puzzle values and the protocol are re-rolled on every retry, so an old answer will not work. Next Shift starts a new station with less reserve and clears the retry count.

title: Power Room
text: The Power room has four breakers, B1 to B4. Each shows a voltage rating chosen from 120, 208, 240, 277, 400 and 480 volts, and the room shows a LOAD MODE of RESTORE or SHED. Aim at a breaker and press E to flip it.

title: Power: Breaker Order
text: Protocol A, RESTORE: flip the breakers from the lowest voltage to the highest. Protocol A, SHED: flip them from the highest voltage to the lowest. Protocol B, RESTORE: flip them from the highest voltage to the lowest. Protocol B, SHED: flip them from the lowest voltage to the highest. A wrong breaker causes a surge that resets all four and costs 15 seconds.

title: Oxygen Room
text: The Oxygen room shows a STATION MODE of NIGHT, DAY or EMERGENCY. Use the console to open the valve controls, set valves A, B and C in steps of 10, then confirm.

title: Oxygen: Valve Settings
text: Set valves A, B and C to these values. Protocol A, NIGHT: 30, 40, 50. Protocol A, DAY: 50, 60, 70. Protocol A, EMERGENCY: 70, 80, 90. Protocol B, NIGHT: 40, 50, 60. Protocol B, DAY: 60, 70, 80. Protocol B, EMERGENCY: 80, 90, 100. Wrong settings cost 10 seconds of reserve.

title: Comms Room
text: The Comms room has a row of six beacons and a frequency tuner, and some of the beacons are lit. Use the console to open the tuner, set a frequency from 100 to 200 MHz in steps of 5, then transmit.

title: Comms: Frequency Formula
text: Protocol A: the distress frequency is 100 MHz plus 20 MHz for every lit beacon, so 3 lit beacons is 160 MHz. Protocol B: the distress frequency is 100 MHz plus 10 MHz for every lit beacon, so 3 lit beacons is 130 MHz. A wrong frequency costs 10 seconds of reserve.

title: Cooling room
text: The Cooling room is the fourth and last room, past Comms. Its door opens once Comms is repaired. A reactor core glows in the room, and a display shows the CORE TEMP in kelvin and the REACTOR state, NORMAL or SURGE. Use the console to open the coolant control, set a flow from 0 to 40 L/s with the buttons, then press Engage Cooling.

title: Cooling formula
text: Protocol A: coolant flow is the core temperature minus 400, divided by 20, in L/s, so 560 K is 8 L/s. Protocol B: the core temperature minus 400, divided by 10, so 560 K is 16 L/s. If the reactor state is SURGE, add 5 L/s to either result. A wrong flow costs 10 seconds of reserve.

title: Cryo Bay
text: The Cryo Bay is an optional room at the west end of the corridor, between the crew quarters and the reboot terminal, so you pass its door on the way to reboot. Its door is never locked. Six pods hold the sleeping crew; they glow red while the station is broken and turn cyan as you repair it. Four terminals show the crew's logs, which tell the story. Reading them pauses the game and changes nothing.

title: Mistake Penalties
text: Mistakes cost reserve time (Engineer values). A wrong breaker (a power surge) costs 15 seconds. Wrong valve settings, a wrong frequency and a wrong coolant flow cost 10 seconds each. The reserve never goes below zero.

title: Reboot Terminal
text: The reboot terminal at the west end of the corridor works only when all four systems are repaired, and it turns cyan when ready. Using it earlier shows a warning. With all four repaired it opens the reboot code; entering the code wins the shift and shows your score (see the reboot code entry). You have to walk all the way back to it.

title: Reboot code
text: With all four systems repaired, the reboot terminal asks for a code. Four pads, A to D, flash in a sequence. Protocol A: press them in the same order. Protocol B: press them in reverse order. The first showing is free; showing it again costs half a hint (10 seconds on Engineer). A wrong pad costs the usual wrong-answer penalty (10 seconds on Engineer) and the sequence is shown again. Later shifts have longer sequences.

title: Doors and Corridor Hazards
text: The doors open in order: Oxygen after Power, Comms after Oxygen, Cooling after Comms. On Engineer, gas vents in the corridor drain the reserve fast while their lamp is red: 12 seconds of reserve for every second in the gas. Wait for a grey lamp; amber is a warning. A laser grid blocks the way past Oxygen; touching it costs 10 seconds. Press E on a wall switch beside it to turn it off for 10 seconds. Hazards are not puzzle mistakes.

title: Hazards grow
text: The corridor gets worse with every shift. Each gas vent is quiet for 0.5 seconds less (down to 1.5) and vents for 0.5 seconds longer (up to 9), and its cloud is 1 metre longer (up to 10). A wall switch keeps a laser grid off 1 second less, never below half its time. From shift 3 a second laser grid blocks the corridor between Comms and Cooling, with its own two switches.

title: Hazards and repairs
text: Repairing a system shuts down the hazard it was feeding. Comms switches off the first laser grid and Cooling the second, for good. Oxygen seals the corridor vent between Power and Oxygen and the gas leak in the Oxygen room; Cooling seals the leak in the Cooling room. The Oxygen room always leaks at its console until Oxygen is repaired; the Cooling room leaks only while the reactor state is SURGE. Wait for the grey lamp. The walk back is safer.

title: Adaptive difficulty
text: After each cleared shift the game adapts the next with a fixed rule, not machine learning. It uses the share of the reserve used (averaged with your last shift), mistakes and retries. Easier: more than 80% used, or 3 retries or 6 mistakes. Harder: under 40% used, at most 1 retry and 2 mistakes. Otherwise balanced. A step is 45 seconds of reserve plus one shift of hazard growth, up to 2 steps easier or 3 harder. Settings can switch it off.

title: About ORACLE
text: ORACLE quotes these manuals exactly for rules and numbers. It cannot see your rooms: not the load mode, the station mode, the number of lit beacons, the core temperature, the breaker voltages or the protocol. Tell it what you read (the breaker voltages, the protocol and the mode) and it works out the order. It cannot change the game. Press H to open it.

title: Offline Play
text: The game works fully offline. ORACLE can also use a small language model that you install separately with Ollama (the model qwen2.5:1.5b). If it is not running, ORACLE shows the matching manual entries instead.

title: Privacy
text: The game collects no personal data and uses no accounts or online services. The only things saved on your computer are your best score and whether you have seen the intro.

title: Levels
text: Pick a level on the main menu: Rookie, Engineer or Survivor. Engineer is the standard game and the other manuals use its numbers. Rookie: 480 s reserve, gas 6 s per second, laser 5 s (off for 15 s), ORACLE free, hint 10 s, penalties 8 and 5 s, score x0.6. Survivor: 270 s reserve, gas 20, laser 20 s (off for 6 s), ORACLE 10 s, hint 40 s, penalties 30 and 20 s, score x1.4.

title: Modifiers
text: Optional extras on the main menu, in any combination. Blackout: the corridor lights flicker and the gas vents start at a different point of their cycle each shift; score x1.15. Hardcore: one failed shift ends the run and clears the run score, and there are no retries; score x1.25. Speedrun: a par time of half the shift's starting reserve is shown under the reserve; beating it gives 100 points plus 1 per second under par.
